_purpose: Re-run UEXP's pre-registered blind Route B labelling with a DIFFERENT model and compare three ways (vs fixture, vs UEXP's labelsB, per-dimension).

replication_detail: kappa 0.858 (this pass) vs 0.901 (UEXP): both >= 0.85, but the exact 0.90 headline does not replicate; pre-registered ladder puts this pass in band 2 on agreement (0.863) and band 1 on kappa.

stratified_kappa._note: vs fixture's recorded labels; B2 = this pass (mimo-v2.6-flash), UEXP = labelsB.json

disagreement_structure.reading: 14-case shared contested core replicates (all four acquisition traps, all four EPHEMERAL/DROP cases, topology-018, capability.family-004/009, context.package-004, worker.class-023, memory.admission-018); tails are reader-specific, not new defects.

memory_admission_convention_detail.convention: step-scoped scratch never re-read: recorded EPHEMERAL vs blind-reader DROP
memory_admission_convention_detail.interpretation: REAL SYSTEMATIC AMBIGUITY at the memory.admission tier boundary, demonstrated with two different blind models - not annotation noise. Top repair item in the fixture.

arity_effect: present and reported for both readers: agreement vs fixture falls from 0.970 (2-option, n=33) to 0.722 (5-option, n=54) for B2 and 1.000 to 0.815 for UEXP; confounded with kind (5-option strata are dominated by memory.admission/acquisition), and NOT consistent with pure option-wording exploitation (model-model kappa 0.9125 on bespoke kinds; B2 scored 28/30 vs UEXP 30/30 on the answer-named escalation stratum). Weakens a blanket 'labels are sound' reading for high-arity closed-roster kinds.
verdict: PARTIAL replication. The magnitude of UEXP's result replicates with a different model (blind kappa 0.858 vs 0.901, both >= 0.85; model-to-model kappa 0.9125), the same dimensions are weak for both readers (memory.admission, acquisition), the 14-case contested core replicates, and the specific systematic finding replicated 4/4: both blind readers say DROP (not EPHEMERAL) on never-re-read step scratch - a REAL fixture ambiguity at the memory.admission tier boundary, the top repair item. What does not replicate: the exact 0.90 headline (second reader lands at 0.863 agreement, band 2 on the pre-registered ladder), and memory.admission kappa degrades to 0.563. Label quality looks robust across models for 6 of 7 kinds, soft for memory.admission, degraded-but-fair for acquisition - not model-specific, but dimension-dependent.
limitation: A MODEL IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT HUMAN ANNOTATOR. Every number here - including the model-to-model kappa of 0.9125 - measures MACHINE reproducibility of the fixture's labels for exactly two models on one fixture, and is NOT inter-annotator agreement. It must never be cited as IAA, does not discharge PAPER_CANDIDATES.md F.3's call for a second independent human labeller, and remains consistent with both models sharing a wrong convention. Replication of a divergence demonstrates ambiguity, not error in either direction.
reproducibility: python3 compare2.py reproduces metrics2.json and disagreementsB2.jsonl from cases.json + labelsB.json + labelsB2.json. UEXP's compare.py was deliberately NOT re-run (it would overwrite UEXP's metrics.json/disagreements.jsonl).
